title: Triangle-free graphs: lazy constraints at partial assignments
description: Graphs on n nodes with at least m edges and no triangle. The abstraction has no triangle constraint; the check finds a triangle, and G.clause(X) adds it as a clause inside the search (lazy constraint generation). With on partial (G5) the check also runs at partial assignments, with the open edges taken as absent (G(P, false)): a triangle among the edges chosen so far cuts the subtree before the candidate is complete. The variant total-only checks total candidates only; every-1 checks at every fixpoint, and several takes up to three triangles per check. Counts checked against clingo with the triangle constraint written out.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Graphs on the nodes 1 .. n.
node(1..n).
pair(X,Y) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a graph with at least m edges. The abstraction does not know the triangles.
{ edge(X,Y) : pair(X,Y) }.
:- #count { X,Y : edge(X,Y) } < m.
#show edge/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a triangle. It depends on its three edges.
1 { tri(X,Y,Z) : node(X), node(Y), node(Z), X < Y, Y < Z } 1.
:- tri(X,Y,Z), not edge(X,Y).
:- tri(X,Y,Z), not edge(X,Z).
:- tri(X,Y,Z), not edge(Y,Z).
relevant(edge(X,Y)) :- tri(X,Y,Z).
relevant(edge(X,Z)) :- tri(X,Y,Z).
relevant(edge(Y,Z)) :- tri(X,Y,Z).
#show tri/3.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Lazy constraint generation: the "no triangle" constraint is not in the abstraction; each
# triangle the check finds becomes a clause, inside the search of A.
search A:
    # G5: also at partial assignments, with the open edges taken as absent (G(P, false)).
    # A triangle found there consists of edges A has already chosen: G.clause(X) is false at
    # once and cuts the subtree. G.clause(X) is sound on a partial candidate: it holds for
    # every graph with these three edges.
    # every 8: at every 8th propagation fixpoint, to keep the number of check calls down.
    on partial P every 8:
        X = C.solve(assume G(P, false))
        if X: reject P with G.clause(X)
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts: % n = 8, at least 16 edges: the 35 complete bipartite graphs K(4,4) (clingo with the triangle constraint).
% n = 7, at least 13 edges: none (at most 12 edges without a triangle).
% n = 6, at least 10 edges: none (at most 9 edges without a triangle, K(3,3)).

variants.name: total-only
variants.loop:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Lazy constraint generation: the "no triangle" constraint is not in the abstraction; each
# triangle the check finds becomes a clause, inside the search of A.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Lazy constraint generation: the "no triangle" constraint is not in the abstraction; each
# triangle the check finds becomes a clause, inside the search of A.
search A:
    # G5: also at partial assignments, with the open edges taken as absent (G(P, false)).
    # A triangle found there consists of edges A has already chosen: G.clause(X) is false at
    # once and cuts the subtree. G.clause(X) is sound on a partial candidate: it holds for
    # every graph with these three edges.
    # every 8: at every 8th propagation fixpoint, to keep the number of check calls down.
    on partial P every 1:
        X = C.solve(assume G(P, false))
        if X: reject P with G.clause(X)
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three triangles per check, each one a clause, at partial and total candidates.
search A:
    on partial P every 8:
        for X in C.models(assume G(P, false), limit 3):
            reject P with G.clause(X)
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

library.summary: Lazy constraint generation at partial assignments (on partial, G(P, false)): graphs with at least m edges and no triangle (n = 8, m = 16, 35 solutions).
